description: Stand up the complete server-side demo infrastructure: Mosquitto MQTT broker, Cloudflare Tunnel, a live browser dashboard, and a hosted JSON config editor. Node-RED removed. Dashboard at mqttfordm.haegens.be/dashboard. Config editor at mqttfordm.haegens.be/editor.

userStories.title: Remove Node-RED from the stack
userStories.description: As a developer, I want Node-RED removed from docker-compose.yml and install.sh so the stack is leaner and there is no confusion about its role.
acceptanceCriteria: nodered service removed from docker-compose.yml
nodered/data directory creation removed from install.sh
Node-RED port 1880 removed from README access URLs table
smoke-test.sh no longer checks port 1880 or the sapdm-nodered container
docker-compose.yml has exactly three services: mosquitto, cloudflared, dashboard
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Add nginx config to serve /dashboard and /editor paths
userStories.description: As a developer, I want the nginx container to serve the dashboard and editor HTML at their respective paths so that Cloudflare path routing works correctly for both.
acceptanceCriteria: dashboard/nginx/default.conf added to repo with a location /dashboard block serving files from /usr/share/nginx/html/dashboard/
dashboard/nginx/default.conf also has a location /editor block serving files from /usr/share/nginx/html/editor/
docker-compose.yml dashboard service mounts ./dashboard/html:/usr/share/nginx/html:ro AND ./dashboard/nginx/default.conf:/etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf:ro
Requesting GET /dashboard/ on port 80 returns HTTP 200
Requesting GET /editor/ on port 80 returns HTTP 200
Requesting GET / on port 80 returns HTTP 404 (root is reserved for Cloudflare WS passthrough)
docker compose config validates without errors
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: The HTML files for dashboard and editor are added in later stories. This story only wires up nginx routing so both paths are ready.

userStories.title: Move editor to /editor path and update cloudflared config
userStories.description: As a developer, I want the existing JSON config editor hosted at /editor so it is reachable remotely via the Cloudflare Tunnel.
acceptanceCriteria: dashboard/html/editor.html moved to dashboard/html/editor/index.html
Requesting GET /editor/ on port 80 returns HTTP 200 with the editor HTML

cloudflared/config.yml.example ingress section updated to three rules in order: (1) hostname mqttfordm.haegens.be path /editor.* → http://dashboard:80; (2) hostname mqttfordm.haegens.be path /dashboard.* → http://dashboard:80; (3) hostname mqttfordm.haegens.be (catch-all, no path) → ws://mosquitto:9001
A comment in config.yml.example explains rule ordering: HTTP path rules must come before the WS catch-all or all traffic goes to Mosquitto
Fallback rule (http_status:404) remains as the final entry for unmatched hostnames
docker compose config validates without errors
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: The editor already exists at dashboard/html/editor.html — this story relocates it and wires up Cloudflare routing. No changes to editor functionality.

userStories.title: Build live MQTT dashboard — connection, feed, and topic table
userStories.description: As an operator, I want to open /dashboard in a browser and see live MQTT messages from the broker so I can verify the ESP32 is publishing correctly.
acceptanceCriteria: dashboard/html/dashboard/index.html created as a single self-contained HTML file
mqtt.js loaded from CDN https://unpkg.com/mqtt/dist/mqtt.min.js — no build step
On load, broker URL is derived as: window.location.protocol === 'https:' ? 'wss://' + window.location.hostname : 'ws://' + window.location.hostname + ':9001'
Connection status indicator shows green 'Connected' with ISO timestamp on connect, red 'Disconnected' on disconnect
Client subscribes to # immediately on connect
Live message feed shows timestamp, topic, payload — newest entry at top, capped at 100 entries, scrollable
Per-topic last-value table updates as messages arrive: columns are Topic, Last Value, Time Ago — sorted alphabetically by topic
Visual style uses IBM Plex Sans and IBM Plex Mono fonts (Google Fonts CDN) and the same SAP Fiori CSS color tokens as dashboard/html/index.html (--hi, --ok, --err, --bg, --tx, etc.)
Page is usable at 1280px+ viewport width
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Publish panel is handled separately in US-005. This story delivers the read-only monitoring view.

userStories.title: Add publish panel to dashboard
userStories.description: As an operator, I want to send MQTT messages from the browser dashboard so I can inject test values without needing mosquitto_pub on the command line.
acceptanceCriteria: Publish panel added to dashboard/html/dashboard/index.html below the topic table
Panel contains: Topic text input (placeholder 'factory/test'), Payload text input, QoS dropdown with options 0 and 1, Publish button
Clicking Publish sends the message via the existing MQTT connection
After a successful publish, the sent message appears in the live feed with a distinct 'OUT' label or color to distinguish it from received messages
If the client is disconnected, the Publish button is disabled and shows 'Not connected'
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Update smoke test for trimmed stack
userStories.description: As a developer, I want the smoke test to validate the updated three-service stack so I can confirm everything is wired up correctly after deploy.
acceptanceCriteria: smoke-test.sh expected container list is exactly: sapdm-mosquitto sapdm-cloudflared sapdm-dashboard
Smoke test checks http://localhost/dashboard/ returns HTTP 200
Smoke test checks http://localhost/editor/ returns HTTP 200
Smoke test still checks MQTT TCP pub/sub round-trip on port 1883
Smoke test still checks WebSocket port 9001 is open with nc
Smoke test still checks Cloudflare Tunnel connectivity as an optional/skip check
Running bash scripts/smoke-test.sh exits 0 when all required checks pass
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Update README and install.sh for new stack
userStories.description: As a new user, I want the README and install.sh to reflect the current three-service stack so I can follow accurate setup instructions.
acceptanceCriteria: README Services table has three rows: Mosquitto, Cloudflared, Dashboard — Node-RED row removed
README dashboard row shows port 80 and paths /dashboard and /editor
README Cloudflare Tunnel setup section updated to describe the three-ingress routing (/editor, /dashboard, WS catch-all)
install.sh runtime directory creation creates only mosquitto/data and mosquitto/log — nodered/data removed
install.sh success output Access URLs section shows: Dashboard at http://<ip>/dashboard/, Editor at http://<ip>/editor/, MQTT TCP at <ip>:1883, MQTT WS at <ip>:9001
Typecheck passes
